item.text:
**8B.3 Research Note**
Assessment: mostly yes, but with an important caveat. Marcos did mobilize the bureaucracy, security apparatus, and parts of the coalition around a fairly coherent 2024 program. The best evidence is the repeated use of executive orders, inter-agency task forces, procurement rules, and campaign-linked alliance management. The caveat is that much of this remained presidency-centered, coalition discipline was personalized rather than party-structural, and broader civic/patronage conditions still blunted clean mobilization.

**Supports**
- [SONA highlights whole-of-government effort to achieve food security, inclusive economic growth - NEDA](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/sona-highlights-whole-of-government-effort-to-achieve-food-security-inclusive-economic-growth-neda/) | Presidential Communications Office / NEDA | 2024-07-23 | Claim: Marcos’s SONA was explicitly framed as a whole-of-government implementation push for the Philippine Development Plan 2023-2028, showing coordinated mobilization of the state behind a named program. | QIDs: 8B.3, 8B.2, 8B.1, 7B.5
- [PBBM issues EO No. 52 institutionalizing and expanding DSWD's Pag-Abot Program](https://mirror.pia.gov.ph/press-releases/2024/01/22/pbbm-issues-eo-no-52-institutionalizing-and-expanding-dswds-pag-abot-program-for-street-dwellers-other-poor-and-vulnerable-individuals) | Presidential Communications Office via PIA | 2024-01-22 | Claim: EO 52 created an inter-agency structure, monitoring system, and reporting cadence for Pag-Abot, which is evidence of bureaucratic mobilization rather than ad hoc patronage. | QIDs: 8B.3, 8B.2, 7B.9
- [PBBM adopts DICT’s National Cybersecurity Plan 2023-2028](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-adopts-dicts-national-cybersecurity-plan-2023-2028/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-06 | Claim: EO 58 converted the cybersecurity plan into a whole-of-nation roadmap and ordered agencies and LGUs to implement, monitor, and report, showing real apparatus mobilization. | QIDs: 8B.3, 8B.2, 7B.8, 7B.9
- [PBBM reorganizes Inter-Agency Task Force on Zero Hunger](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-reorganizes-inter-agency-task-force-on-zero-hunger/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-08-09 | Claim: Marcos reshuffled the zero-hunger task force to broaden membership and ensure continued implementation, showing the use of a formal coordination mechanism to push the food-security program. | QIDs: 8B.3, 8B.2, 7B.5
- [PBBM sets streamlined permitting for PH infra flagship projects](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-sets-streamlined-permitting-for-ph-infra-flagship-projects/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-05-04 | Claim: EO 59 directed national agencies and LGUs to streamline permits for infrastructure flagship projects, a concrete example of mobilizing bureaucracy toward execution speed. | QIDs: 8B.3, 8B.2
- [PBBM signs laws on streamlining procurement, combatting online scams](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-20 | Claim: Procurement reform standardized forms and institutionalized e-procurement, turning the state’s purchasing machinery into a more centrally directed delivery tool. | QIDs: 8B.3, 8B.2, 7B.9, 7B.10
- [PBBM orders agencies to help COS, JO workers get permanent positions in government](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-agencies-to-help-cos-jo-workers-get-permanent-positions-in-government/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-25 | Claim: Marcos used executive direction to push agencies to regularize long-serving workers through qualification and training, which is direct administrative mobilization. | QIDs: 8B.3, 8B.2, 7B.9
- [PBBM stands by suspension of 139 NFA officials](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-stands-by-suspension-of-139-nfa-officials/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-03-06 | Claim: Marcos backed enforcement against anomalous rice-sales officials, showing that the bureaucracy could be disciplined and redirected when it misfired. | QIDs: 8B.3, 8B.2, 7B.9, 7B.10
- [PBBM refutes alleged loophole in EO 74, reiterates POGO ban in all forms](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-refutes-alleged-loophole-in-eo-74-reiterates-pogo-ban-in-all-forms/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-11-11 | Claim: Marcos closed off loophole arguments around the POGO ban, which is evidence of enforcement follow-through against a politically sensitive rent stream. | QIDs: 8B.3, 8B.2, 7B.9, 7B.10
- [PBBM calls for comprehensive national flood-control plan to protect communities, production areas](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-calls-for-comprehensive-national-flood-control-plan-to-protect-communities-production-areas/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-26 | Claim: Marcos used the flood crisis to mobilize agencies around a national mitigation plan and swift assistance, showing state apparatus activation around a priority. | QIDs: 8B.3, 8B.2, 7B.5
- [Marcos’s economic managers publicly set out macro strategy in forum](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1228524) | Philippine News Agency | 2024-07-08 | Claim: The economic team coordinated publicly across NEDA, BSP, DBM, Treasury, and the investment office, which is good evidence of technocratic mobilization behind the chosen macro program. | QIDs: 8B.3, 8B.2, 7B.5
- [Marcos-Romualdez parties forge political alliance](https://www.bworldonline.com/the-nation/2024/05/08/593686/marcos-romualdez-parties-forge-political-alliance/) | BusinessWorld Online | 2024-05-08 | Claim: The Marcos and Romualdez parties formed a formal alliance for the 2025 midterms, showing active coalition building around the ruling network. | QIDs: 8B.3, 7B.9, 7B.10
- [PBBM reorganizes NSC to be a resilient national security institution](https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2024/eo_81_2024.html) | Lawphil / Office of the President | 2024-12-30 | Claim: EO 81 reworked the National Security Council into a more coordinated security institution, though still with strong presidential discretion, showing late-year security mobilization. | QIDs: 8B.3, 8B.2

**Counters**
- [Philippines: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Claim: Freedom House says campaign-finance rules are weak and poorly enforced, and patronage/kinship still shape politics, which means the ruling network was not mobilized through clean, programmatic channels alone. | QIDs: 8B.3, 7B.9, 7B.10
- [Philippines: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Claim: The report says the government and allied actors manipulated online information and retained inherited site blocks, suggesting mobilization relied partly on coercive information control. | QIDs: 8B.3, 7B.9, 7B.10
- [Philippines | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | Claim: Red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and regulatory pressure on broadcasters persisted, so the state’s mobilization remained partly coercive and not fully rule-bound. | QIDs: 8B.3, 7B.9, 7B.10
- [No PH cooperation with ICC unless PRRD wants it - PBBM](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/no-ph-cooperation-with-icc-unless-prrd-wants-it-pbbm/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-11-14 | Claim: Marcos refused independent ICC cooperation on the Duterte drug war unless Duterte consented, which shows selective accountability and limits on how far he would mobilize the state for external scrutiny. | QIDs: 8B.3, 7B.7, 7B.10
- [NEDA said the rice tariff cut did not reduce retail rice prices as anticipated](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/economy/929579/neda-reduced-rice-tariffs-failed-to-lower-prices/story/) | GMA News Online | 2024-12-10 | Claim: The flagship rice intervention only partly worked, showing that some mobilization translated into incomplete execution and weak pass-through. | QIDs: 8B.3, 8B.2, 7B.5
- [TeleRadyo JV with Prime Media / regulatory pressure persists](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | Claim: The report notes a Romualdez-linked media joint venture and continued regulatory pressure over broadcasters, suggesting the ruling network still depended on politically connected leverage. | QIDs: 8B.3, 7B.9, 7B.10

**Search gap**
- I did not find a public internal dashboard or party-whip record that shows how tightly the Marcos coalition was managed month by month.
- The evidence is strongest for presidency-centered bureaucracy and security coordination. It is weaker for durable party discipline, because the ruling bloc still looks family- and alliance-driven rather than institutionally party-based.
- The main unresolved question is whether the same mobilization would hold without Marcos’s personal direction.
